You are auditing citations in a law review manuscript. REPO ROOT: /home/user/projects/mirror

SCOPE (do not stray outside it): section "Introduction" of `paper/typst/body-src.typ`, LINES 5-30. That range contains approximately 13 `#cite(<Key>)` calls.

READ-ONLY on the manuscript. Do NOT edit body-src.typ, body.typ, sources.bib, cite-data.typ, or anything else in the repo. Your ONLY write is your report file.

STEP 1 — enumerate. Read lines 5-30 of `paper/typst/body-src.typ` (use `sed -n '5,30p'` or Read with offset/limit). Extract EVERY `#cite(<Key>...)` occurrence, in order. For each record: (i) line number, (ii) bib key, (iii) the `supplement:` pincite if present (e.g. `supplement: [2071--72]`), (iv) the CLAIM it supports — the surrounding footnote text or, if the cite is bare, the sentence in the body that carries the footnote. Cites live inside `#footnote[...]`; the claim is the body sentence the footnote hangs off of, plus any parenthetical gloss in the footnote itself.

STEP 2 — bib check. For each key, find its entry in `paper/references/sources.bib`. Verify: entry exists; author, title, year, journal/publisher, volume, and page fields are present and internally consistent (e.g. a 2019 article cited for "as of 2019" figures; a journal article has volume+pages; a news item has a date and outlet). Flag placeholder/stub entries, obviously wrong years, duplicated-looking entries. NOTE: `paper/references/sources.bib` IS the "refs.bib" for this project — there is no file literally named refs.bib.

STEP 3 — source check. Each bib entry should have a corresponding file in `paper/references/` (e.g. `Bebchuk2019-uq.pdf`, `Macey2026-bs.md`). Find it (`ls paper/references/`). Extract text (`pdftotext -layout <f> -` for PDFs, `cat` for .md/.html/.xml) and verify the source ACTUALLY SUPPORTS the claim. If a pincite page/page-range is given, check that the cited page exists in the document and that the supporting language is at/near it. Quote the supporting sentence from the source verbatim (<=40 words) as evidence. If you cannot find support, say so plainly — do not invent a quote.

STEP 4 — verdict per citation, one of:
  OK              — claim supported, metadata sound, pincite correct
  PINCITE-WRONG   — supported but the page/pin is wrong or unverifiable
  WEAK            — source is topically relevant but does not squarely support the stated proposition
  UNSUPPORTED     — source does not support the claim
  METADATA-WRONG  — bib entry has a wrong/missing field
  SOURCE-MISSING  — no source file in paper/references/ to check against

STEP 5 — write the report to EXACTLY this path: `/home/user/projects/mirror/paper/scratch/cite-check/01-introduction.md`

Format:

Then a `## Issues` section listing ONLY the non-OK rows, each with 2-4 sentences of detail and a concrete suggested fix (drop the cite, swap the key, change the pincite to X, reword the claim to Y).
Then a `## Coverage` section stating exactly which cites you verified against the underlying source text and which you could not, and why.

HONESTY REQUIREMENTS (these matter more than a tidy table):
- Never report a verdict you did not actually check. If you ran out of ability to check one, mark it and say so in Coverage.
- Never fabricate a quotation, page number, or bib field. Quote only text you actually read from the file.
- If the count of cites you find differs from the ~13 stated above, report YOUR count and note the discrepancy.
